bull.b: Snowflake’s cloud-native, multi-cloud data platform and consumption pricing create durable monetization: customers centralize data and pay as they scale, enabling high expansion potential across workloads (warehousing, lakehouse, AI/ML). This structural model supports long-term revenue per customer and cross-sell.

Sustained double-digit product revenue growth alongside 126% net revenue retention signals strong account expansion and stickiness. Durable expansion within large customers (more $10M and $1M spenders) underpins predictable, recurring consumption growth over the medium term.

Consistent positive operating and free cash flow provides financial flexibility for R&D, go-to-market investment, buybacks and acquisitions. Strong cash conversion despite GAAP losses reduces solvency risk and supports strategic investments in AI and platform expansion over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Leverage has increased materially from prior low levels, raising interest and refinancing risk while equity remains suppressed by losses. Higher debt reduces capital flexibility for inorganic growth or margin cushioning and increases financial vulnerability during macro or execution slowdowns.

Attractive gross economics are offset by persistent operating losses, producing a deeply negative net margin. Until operating expense intensity is sustainably controlled, GAAP losses constrain return on equity and make durable shareholder value generation more dependent on continued high growth and margin improvement.

Rapid scaling of lower-margin AI consumption, plus acquisition-related ~150bp headwind and Q4 booking concentration, can compress overall margins and make revenue timing lumpy. Customers may also throttle usage for cost control, limiting expected consumption-driven upside.
